topic.subject: social
topic.title: New questions and ideas
topic.scope: the Buddha, Mahavira, Upanishads, sangha, viharas, Jainism and Buddhism teachings

misconceptions.statement: The Upanishads were written by the Buddha to teach people how to pray.
misconceptions.why: Students often conflate all ancient religious texts as belonging to the same historical figure or movement.
misconceptions.fix: The Upanishads are part of the later Vedic tradition, which existed before the Buddha and focused on philosophical discussions about the soul and the universe.

misconceptions.statement: Jainism teaches that you must hurt insects to protect your crops.
misconceptions.why: Students misinterpret the extreme focus on ahimsa (non-violence) as being impractical or contradictory to daily survival.
misconceptions.fix: Jainism emphasizes ahimsa, which means not harming any living being, including insects, which is why followers often avoid farming or take extreme care.

probe.question: Why do Jains avoid farming?
probe.wrong_answer: Because they want to kill insects to save their crops.

misconceptions.statement: The Buddha was a god who created the world.
misconceptions.why: Students project their understanding of modern deities onto historical figures who are worshipped.
misconceptions.fix: The Buddha was a human teacher who sought to end suffering through meditation and right living, not a creator god.

probe.question: What did the Buddha create?
probe.wrong_answer: He created the world and all living things.

misconceptions.statement: Viharas were built as palaces for kings to live in.
misconceptions.why: The grand architecture of ancient stone structures leads students to assume they were royal residences.
misconceptions.fix: Viharas were monasteries or shelters built for monks to live and study during the rainy season.

probe.question: Who lived in a vihara?
probe.wrong_answer: The king and his royal family.
